phylojunction.interface.grammar.ct_fn_treereader_makers module

phylojunction.interface.grammar.ct_fn_treereader_makers.make_tree_reader(ct_fn_name: str, ct_fn_param_dict: Dict[str, List[str | NodeDAG]]) → ConstantFn

Parse ‘read_tree’s arguments and build a ‘CtFnTreeReader’.

This is the only place that can tell “the user wrote ‘n=1’” apart from “the user did not write ‘n’ at all, so it defaulted to 1” – ‘ct_fn_param_dict’ either has an ‘n’/’nr’ key or it does not, whereas by the time a plain ‘int’ value reaches ‘CtFnTreeReader’ itself, that distinction is already lost. ‘n_provided’/ ‘nr_provided’ (below) capture it here and thread it through, so ‘CtFnTreeReader’ can tell its own two cases apart – see its own docstring for what each one does.

Parameters:

  • ct_fn_name (str) – Name of the constant function being called (always ‘read_tree’).

  • ct_fn_param_dict (dict) – Dictionary containing constant function parameter names (str) as keys and lists (of either strings or NodeDAGs) as values.

Returns:

A ‘CtFnTreeReader’ instance, ready to

’.generate()’ one or more AnnotatedTree(s).

Return type:

(ConstantFn)

phylojunction.interface.grammar.det_fn_branch_count_makers module

phylojunction.interface.grammar.det_fn_branch_count_makers.make_n_rec_branches(det_fn_name: str, det_fn_param_dict: Dict[str, List[str | NodeDAG]]) → List[int]

Build and return the number of branches of each tree in ‘tree’.

Called when the ‘:=’ operator is used together with the ‘n_rec_branches’ deterministic function, e.g.:

n_br := n_rec_branches(tree=trs)

One int per tree held by the ‘tree’ argument’s DAG node, in the same (sample, replicate) order, counting only real branches of each tree’s reconstructed topology – see ‘tree.is_real_branch’ for exactly what that excludes (the root, and any zero-length branch), and ‘AnnotatedTree.n_rec_branches’ for the counting itself. Because this is pure tree-topology bookkeeping (no randomness involved), the result can in principle differ for every (sample, replicate) tree, even within the same sample.

This is meant to be usable on its own (e.g., for summary statistics), but is also the building block for feeding per-branch base rates into a clock model – see ‘interface.grammar.dn_grammar’s ‘n_nr_from’ argument, which can point a parametric distribution (e.g. ‘lognormal’) at this det-fn’s output so it draws one value per branch, per tree.

Parameters:

  • det_fn_name (str) – Name of the deterministic function being called (always ‘n_rec_branches’).

  • det_fn_param_dict (dict) – Dictionary containing deterministic function parameter names (str) as keys and lists (of either strings or NodeDAGs) as values.

Returns:

One branch count per tree in ‘tree’, in the

same order.

Return type:

(list of int)

phylojunction.interface.grammar.det_fn_clock_makers module

phylojunction.interface.grammar.det_fn_clock_makers.make_gamma_spike_clock_tree(det_fn_name: str, det_fn_param_dict: Dict[str, List[str | NodeDAG]]) → List[AnnotatedTree]

Build and return trees annotated by a Gamma-spike clock model.

Called when the ‘:=’ operator is used together with the ‘gamma_spike_clock’ deterministic function, e.g.:

n_br := n_rec_branches(tree=trs) br_specific_rel_rate ~ lognormal(n_nr_from=n_br, meanlog=-0.08, sdlog=0.4, log_space=”true”) phylo := gamma_spike_clock(tree=trs, attr_name=”mutation_rate”, clock_rate=0.01, br_specific_rel_rate=br_specific_rel_rate, spike_mean=0.01, spike_shape=2.0, strict_clock_when_no_stubs=”true”)

There is no ‘seed’ parameter: reproducibility is controlled once, globally, for the whole DAG (see ‘calculation.gamma_spike_clock_model.populate_gamma_spike_mol_rates_on_rec_tr_branches’ for why).

‘br_specific_rel_rate’ is required: a DAG node already holding one pre-generated list of per-branch relative rates per tree in ‘tree’ – dimensionless multipliers, conventionally centered at 1.0 in real space (e.g., a ‘lognormal(meanlog=-sdlog**2/2, …)’ node, so that ‘clock_rate’ alone remains the mean absolute rate – the same identifiability convention BEAST2’s UCLN relaxed clock uses), e.g. built with ‘lognormal(n_nr_from=n_br, …)’, where ‘n_br := n_rec_branches(tree=trs)’. This model never draws the gradual, relaxed-clock component internally – its own hyperparameters (and the distribution used) are always chosen independently, in the script. See ‘calculation.gamma_spike_clock_model.populate_gamma_spike_mol_rates_on_rec_tr_branches’s ‘br_specific_rel_rates’ parameter for exactly how these are consumed (the spike component is always still drawn internally here).

‘strict_clock_when_no_stubs’ is optional (a quoted ‘“true”’ or ‘“false”’ string; defaults to ‘“false”’ if not given) – see ‘calculation.gamma_spike_clock_model.populate_gamma_spike_mol_rates_on_rec_tr_branches’ for what it does. NOTE: setting it to ‘“true”’ is NOT a realistic model of molecular evolution; it is a debugging/diagnostic device only (again, see that function’s docstring), not something to use for actual analyses.

Parameters:

  • det_fn_name (str) – Name of the deterministic function being called (always ‘gamma_spike_clock’).

  • det_fn_param_dict (dict) – Dictionary containing deterministic function parameter names (str) as keys and lists (of either strings or NodeDAGs) as values.

Returns:

One new tree per tree held by the

’tree’ argument’s DAG node, each annotated by a ‘GammaSpikeClockModel’.

Return type:

(list of AnnotatedTree)
